problemStatement.formal: For continuous f on [a,b] with f(a) ≤ 0 ≤ f(b), for any ε > 0, bisection produces x ∈ [a,b] with |f(x)| < ε
problemStatement.plain: The constructive content of the Intermediate Value Theorem: bisection provides an algorithm to compute approximate roots to any desired precision. Rather than just asserting existence (∃ x, f(x) = 0), this formalization constructs the root via bisection and proves convergence.
whyMatters: Bridges classical existence proof with constructive computation
Formalizes one of the most fundamental numerical algorithms
Demonstrates how uniform continuity on compact sets yields convergence

proven: Sign invariant maintained through all bisection steps
Left endpoint non-decreasing, right endpoint non-increasing
Approximate IVT: for any ε > 0, bisection finds x with |f(x)| < ε
Uniqueness of zero for strictly monotone functions
knownResults.goal: Fully verified constructive IVT via bisection

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Full constructive IVT formalization with 13 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Bisection algorithm with width bounds, sign preservation, containment, approximate IVT, and monotone uniqueness.
builtItems: approx_ivt: main theorem - approximate root finding via uniform continuity
monotone_ivt_unique: uniqueness for strictly monotone functions
constructive_ivt_summary: combined result packaging all three properties
insights: bisectStep must inline midpoint computation (no let binding) to enable split_ifs tactic
bisect_left_mono and bisect_right_mono require ordering hypothesis p.1 ≤ p.2
Key proof technique: uniform continuity on compact [a,b] gives δ for any ε, then choose n so (b-a)/2^n < δ
exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one provides the Archimedean step for choosing n
